Class NlsBundleGuard

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.nls.NlsBundleGuard
public final class NlsBundleGuard extends Object
Checks that one messages*.properties bundle pair satisfies the rules the delivered NLS payload depends on.

The checks return a list of violations instead of asserting, so that the same implementation can back the guard in grafiosch-base (which sees only the library bundle) and the guard in grafioschtrader-server (which sees both bundles), and so that a failure reports every problem at once rather than only the first.

  • Method Details

    • checkBundlePair

      public static List<String> checkBundlePair(String bundleBaseName, Set<String> enReuseAllowlist)
      Runs every per-bundle-pair check.
      Parameters:
      bundleBaseName - class path base name, for example NlsBundleInspector.BASE_BUNDLE
      enReuseAllowlist - keys whose German value may deliberately equal the English one
      Returns:
      one description per violation, empty when the pair is sound

    • checkDuplicates

      public static List<String> checkDuplicates(NlsBundleInspector.Bundle bundle)
      A key must occur at most once per file. Properties.load(Reader) keeps the last occurrence silently, so a duplicate is invisible at runtime and shows up only as a text that will not change no matter which entry is edited.

    • checkKeyCharset

      public static List<String> checkKeyCharset(NlsBundleInspector.Bundle bundle)
      A key must be expressible in .properties syntax without escaping, so the files stay readable and a key can be grepped for as written.

    • checkParity

      public static List<String> checkParity(NlsBundleInspector.Bundle english, NlsBundleInspector.Bundle german)
      Both languages must define exactly the same keys. The English bundle stays the ResourceBundle fallback, so a gap would surface as an English text rather than as an error; strict parity at build time is what guarantees no such gap ever reaches a user.

    • checkEnReuse

      public static List<String> checkEnReuse(NlsBundleInspector.Bundle english, NlsBundleInspector.Bundle german, Set<String> enReuseAllowlist)
      A German value identical to the English one is usually a forgotten translation. Where it is deliberate, such as a provider's subscription tier name, the key is listed in the module's nls-en-reuse.txt. A stale entry is a violation too, so the allow list cannot silently accumulate keys that have since been translated or removed.

    • checkPlaceholderDialect

      public static List<String> checkPlaceholderDialect(NlsBundleInspector.Bundle bundle)
      The two placeholder dialects must not be mixed on one key. Values resolved server-side pass through MessageFormat, which uses {0} and treats a single quote as an escape character; values resolved by ngx-translate in the browser use {{name}} and take a single quote literally. A key that mixes them renders wrongly on at least one of the two paths.
